'''Victoria E. Howle''' is an American applied mathematician specializing in [[numerical linear algebra]]. She is known as one of the developers of the [[Trilinos]] open-source software library for scientific computing<ref>{{Cite web |title=Documentation {{!}} Trilinos |url=https://trilinos.github.io/documentation.html |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=trilinos.github.io |language=en}}</ref>. She is a full professor in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at
[[Texas Tech University]].<ref name="cv" />

==Education and career==
Howle graduated from [[Rutgers University]] in 1988 with a bachelor's degree in English literature.{{r|cv}} She earned her Ph.D. in 2001 from [[Cornell University]]. Her dissertation, ''Efficient Iterative Methods for Ill-Conditioned Linear and Nonlinear Network Problems'', was supervised by Stephen Vavasis.{{r|mg}}

After working as a researcher at [[Sandia National Laboratories]] from 2000 to 2007, she took a faculty position at Texas Tech in 2007.{{r|cv}}

==Service and recognition==
Howle was one of the inaugural winners of the [[AWM Service Award]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in 2013.{{r|awm|awm2}} The award honored her service to the association, including founding its annual essay contest in which students write biographies of contemporary women mathematicians.{{r|cv|awm2}}
